script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 13. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You can survive weeks without food.  Days without water.  But only minutes without oxygen.

Inside each cell, tiny structures called mitochondria combine oxygen with glucose to produce ATP—the energy currency of life. This process is called cellular respiration. You're not just breathing; you're running trillions of tiny engines. Your brain is an oxygen hog.  It weighs only 2% of your body but consumes 20% of your oxygen.

Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Everything requires energy, and energy requires fuel.  Oxygen reminds us that what seems effortless—breathing, thinking, being—depends on constant supply chains we rarely notice.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Energy Audit - What Fuels You?.

Here's your activity: Just as cells need oxygen, you need certain things to function. What are your essential fuels—sleep, connection, purpose, movement? Are you getting enough? Identify one fuel you're running low on and plan to replenish it. This helps you identify and protect your essential fuel sources.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why we need oxygen can be applied to energy audit - what fuels you?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
